headline: Natural Gas Plummets and WTI Crude Dips on Demand and Supply Shifts
paragraphs: Natural gas prices cratered 5.70 percent on the day and plunged 12.63 percent over the week as weather demand dropped. WTI crude fell 4.51 percent on the day, reversing initial gains as traders weighed a Gulf supply recovery, though it held a weekly gain of 2.22 percent. Brent crude remained little changed up 0.05 percent daily and up 2.62 percent weekly as traders assessed Middle East developments and weighed Gulf supply recovery against record tanker rates.

Gold rose 0.33 percent on the day and 1.17 percent for the week to EUR 3697.68, holding critical support near $4,110 despite rising bond yields and a strengthening dollar. Silver showed resilience with a 4.10 percent weekly gain to EUR 51.45, supported by record ETF holdings. Copper edged up 0.39 percent on the day to EUR 5.86, despite broader reports of rising inventories and easing supply worries. The euro stood at 1.1240 against the US dollar.
